author: joaquinbejar
body:
Market hierarchy persistence, DOUBLE PRECISION migration, and improved position closing (v0.2.0)

Description

This pull request delivers first-class PostgreSQL persistence for IG market hierarchy data, upgrades numeric storage to DOUBLE PRECISION, and hardens position-closing behavior to align with IG’s API. It also enhances the trade example with realistic lifecycle tests and observability, adds client-side filtering for open positions, and bumps the crate version to 0.2.0 with dependency updates.

The database work introduces schema, views, and indexes optimized for hierarchical queries and instrument lookups. The numeric migration replaces DECIMAL with DOUBLE PRECISION across market_instruments for better performance and practical precision. On the API side, close_position now uses POST with _method=DELETE, adds richer error handling, and ensures Option fields are skipped during serialization when None. Examples and tests validate closing flows by both position ID and epic, with detailed logging.

⸻

Changes Made

Database & Persistence
	•	Added PostgreSQL integration:
	•	market_persistence.rs and market_database.rs.
	•	market_hierarchy_schema.sql with tables, indexes, triggers, and views for efficient hierarchy storage and querying.
	•	Numeric migration:
	•	Replaced DECIMAL with DOUBLE PRECISION in market_instruments and related indexes.
	•	Added migrate_to_double_precision.sql migration script.
	•	Introduced test_database_types.rs example to validate compatibility.
	•	Examples & artifacts:
	•	Added market_hierarchy_to_db.rs example to persist IG Markets data.
	•	Removed market_hierarchy_backup.json; updated .gitignore to exclude any local backups.

Core Library & Services
	•	Position closing:
	•	Refactored close_position to use POST with _method: DELETE for IG API compliance, with detailed error handling.
	•	In ClosePositionRequest, Option<T> fields now skip serialization when None.
	•	Added comments regarding limit order levels in close_option_to_market_by_id.
	•	Query helpers & parsing:
	•	Added get_positions_w_filter to retrieve and client-side filter open positions (with debug logging).
	•	Simplified parse_update_time_utc and parse_period control flow.
	•	Versioning & deps:
	•	Bumped crate to 0.2.0 (previously 0.1.22 during the series) and updated dependencies in Cargo.toml, README.md, and src/lib.rs.

Examples, Tests & Tooling
	•	trade example:
	•	Added dependencies: nanoid, chrono.
	•	Added close_position_test.rs covering creation → verification → closure flows (by ID and by epic) with detailed logging/validation.
	•	Test hygiene:
	•	Marked a long-running test with #[ignore].
	•	Added type annotations in test authenticator to ensure lifetime consistency.
	•	Expanded database statistics struct docs for clarity.

⸻

Testing
	•	Unit/Example Tests
	•	trade/examples/close_position_test.rs: validates lifecycle flows (create, verify, close by ID/epic).
	•	examples/test_database_types.rs: checks runtime compatibility with DOUBLE PRECISION.
	•	Integration/Manual
	•	Verified database schema creation, inserts, and lookups using market_hierarchy_to_db.rs.
	•	Exercised get_positions_w_filter with various filter strings to confirm narrowing and logging.
	•	Manually exercised close_position using POST + _method=DELETE; confirmed server responses and improved error messages.

Suggested commands

# DB migration
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/migrate_to_double_precision.sql

# Run database persistence example
cargo run --example market_hierarchy_to_db --features postgres

# Run example tests (including ignored tests explicitly if needed)
cargo test --examples
cargo test -- --ignored

# Trade example lifecycle tests
cargo test -p trade --test close_position_test


⸻

Screenshots/Examples (Optional)

// Client-side filter usage
let positions = account_service.get_positions_w_filter(Some("EUR/USD".into())).await?;
assert!(positions.iter().all(|p| p.epic.contains("EUR")));

// Close to market by ID (request fields skip None)
ClosePositionRequest {
    deal_id: Some("ABC123".into()),
    limit_level: None,
    stop_level: None,
    // ...
}


⸻

Additional Notes
	•	Breaking change (DB): Switching DECIMAL → DOUBLE PRECISION may affect rounding/precision-sensitive workflows and ORMs. Run the provided migration and review downstream consumers.
	•	API behavior: close_position now uses POST with _method=DELETE. Ensure any proxies or middleware allow method override semantics.
	•	Artifacts: market_hierarchy_backup.json was removed to avoid shipping large example data; generate locally if needed using the provided example.
	•	Follow-ups (nice-to-haves):
	•	Configurable server-side filters for positions to reduce client memory/CPU.
	•	Revisit indexes after real-world workloads.
	•	Consolidate error types for account/market services.

⸻

References
	•	Branch: feature/hierarchy
	•	Key commits:
	•	v0.2.0 & deps: 656b602c
	•	Close flows/tests & example deps: ec55f94f, f6373e5
	•	Serialization & docs for close: 48044c0
	•	IG API compliance for close: c1ce2a4
	•	DB persistence & schema: 872ab42, a4bab3c
	•	DOUBLE PRECISION migration: fe92399
	•	Filtering method: e2606ed
	•	Parsing & test hygiene: 79e28d1
	•	Artifact cleanup & ignore: 63c32b4, a199439
	•	Earlier version bump: 26bb82f

⸻

Checklist
	•	Code changes implemented and self-reviewed.
	•	Database schema and migration script included.
	•	Unit/example tests added and pass locally.
	•	Documentation updated (README.md, README_DATABASE.md).

	•	Migration notes communicated to downstream consumers.
	•	DBA review of schema/indexing.

body:
## Problem

The restaurant's dough allocation and order management system had several critical issues:

1. **Dough allocation only updated after seating, not confirmation** - Reserved pizza counts weren't updated when reservations were confirmed, only when guests were seated
2. **Inaccurate walk-in calculations** - The system wasn't accounting for `pizza_used` in daily supplies, causing walk-in numbers to be incorrect
3. **Duplicate orders from double-clicks** - Frontend lacked protection against rapid button clicks and poor network responses
4. **Missing universal reservation updates** - No robust API for updating reservations with proper dough recalculation
5. **Print server failures breaking orders** - Offline printers would cause entire orders to fail
6. **Incomplete dough recalculation triggers** - Changes to party size, reservation cancellations, and status changes didn't trigger recalculation

## Solution

### Core Logic Improvements

**Enhanced `includes/dough_allocation.php`:**
- Added `incrementDailyPizzaUsed()` function for atomic pizza consumption tracking
- Modified walk-in calculation to include pizza_used: `max(0, pizza_total - pizza_reserved - pizza_used)`
- Added backward compatibility for databases missing the `pizza_used` column

**Improved `includes/reservations_lib.php`:**
- Enhanced `updateReservation()` with comprehensive recalculation triggers
- Now handles status changes, party size modifications, and date moves properly
- Triggers recalc for confirmed ↔ cancelled transitions, not just seated

### API Endpoints

**New `pizza/api/orders/create.php`:**
- Robust order creation with transaction safety
- Print error isolation - orders succeed even if printer fails
- Atomic pizza consumption updates using `incrementDailyPizzaUsed()`

**New `pizza/api/reservations/update.php`:**
- Dedicated reservation update endpoint using the enhanced `updateReservation()` function
- Consistent JSON responses with proper error handling

### Frontend Robustness

**Enhanced `pizza/index.html`:**
```javascript
let submittingOrder = false;  // Prevent double-clicks
async function submitOrder() {
    if (submittingOrder) return;  // Guard against rapid clicks
    submittingOrder = true;
    
    try {
        // Robust JSON parsing with fallback error handling
        const responseText = await response.text();
        const orderResponse = JSON.parse(responseText);
        
        // Handle printer unavailable gracefully
        if (orderResponse.printer_unavailable) {
            showMsg('✅ Objednávka přijata (tisk nedostupný)', true);
        }
    } finally {
        submittingOrder = false;  // Always reset flag
    }
}
```

## Testing Scenarios Verified

All requested scenarios now work correctly:

- ✅ **Pending → Confirmed**: Pizza reserved increases, walk-in decreases immediately
- ✅ **Party size changes**: Instant recalculation for today's confirmed reservations  
- ✅ **Confirmed → Cancelled**: Allocation properly released
- ✅ **New orders**: Pizza_used increases, walk-in decreases by pizza count
- ✅ **Printer offline**: Orders succeed with `printer_unavailable: true` flag
- ✅ **Unchanged reservations**: Returns `{ok: true, unchanged: true}`
- ✅ **Reservation moves**: Recalc triggered when moving to/from today

## Key Features

- **Transaction safety**: Proper rollback handling with `inTransaction()` guards
- **Atomic operations**: Pizza consumption updates are atomic and consistent
- **Error isolation**: Print failures don't affect order creation
- **Double-click prevention**: Frontend protection against rapid submissions
- **Comprehensive logging**: Better debugging with detailed error logs
- **Backward compatibility**: Graceful handling of missing database columns

The system now provides accurate real-time dough allocation tracking and robust order processing that handles network issues and hardware failures gracefully.

Rebase auf master von #524, weil die design_40 template resolution sich geändert hatte.

kivitendo Secrets Vault! Angeregt von @maxwhosevillage .

Die Implementation ist größtenteils in SL::DB::Secret. Ich habe versucht das nach besten crypto Wissen und Gewissen zu implementieren, bin aber höchstens Hobbyist, deshalb gerne reviewen bitte:

- Das Master Passwort wird aus der kivitendo.conf gelesen und mit einem zufälligen Salt per PBKDF2 auf einen 256bit AES key gestreckt, der nur für diesen Eintrag gilt.
- Die eigentliche Ver-/Entschlüsselung passiert mit AES256 im Counter Mode. Counter Mode wurde gewählt, weil der kein Padding braucht und wir auch keine HMAC brauchen (sonst hätte ich GCM genommen).
- Alle Primitive stammen aus CryptX, was auch als neue Abhängigkeit in SL::InstallationCheck steht.
- CryptX hatte im Juni eine CVE aus der unterliegenden tomcrypt lib, deshalb ist eine Minimum-Version 0.065 gefordert.
- Secrets und Master Key sind utf8 aware.
- Beim Entschlüsseln wird statt dem Klartext eine Password Closure zurückgegeben, um ausversehenes Dumpen in Log Files zu verhindern.
- Achtung: Die Parameter für PBKDF2 sind aus den aktuellen OWASP Recommendations genommen und dementsprechend absichtlich teuer. encrypt/decrypt dauert auf meinem ollen i7 Sandy Bridge etwas über eine Sekunde.

Das Frontend ist mit SimpleSystemSettings gebaut, und liegt unter System direkt nach den Hintergrundjobs.
@kiviniklas  : Mir ist dabei ein SimpleSystemSettings Bug aufgefallen, dass der templates nur in templates/webpages sucht. Ich hab das kurz umgebogen auf den echten Template Mechanismus in SL::Presenter.

Zuletzt gibt es noch eine experimentelle (und ungetestete) Applikation davon im ImportRecordEmails BackgroundJob, damit man sieht wie das zu benutzen gedacht ist.
